text: Studying for finals late at night, I need calm music that won't distract me.

summary:
I'm weighing a handful of focus playlists, with classical leaning as the pick for studying, though its melancholy tone gives me pause. I'm also wondering whether lyrics would distract, and I'm leaning toward instrumental music.

I'm also going to pull notes on both the classical and the lyric-free picks before deciding.
There are no notes on Orbit Bloom, Elena Varga, or Slow Stereo, though there are genre notes for them. I'll go with entries 9, 4, 6, 22, and 12, and keep the story between 40 and 90 words.

input.title: Quiet Hours Before Finals

picks.why: A steady, focused lo-fi loop that holds your attention on the page instead of the music.
Soft beats and recorded library rain, made for exactly this kind of late-night study session.
Low-energy ambient texture that fills the silence without asking you to listen closely.
Hushed nylon-string bossa nova for a gentle reset between chapters.
Slow, rippling piano that keeps the room calm while you work through the last pages.

input.story: Every pick here is music you can hear without having to follow it. Lo-fi took the dusty beats of producers like J Dilla and Nujabes and softened them into loops that became a study soundtrack, and Paper Lanterns add rain recorded outside their university library. Brian Eno described ambient as music you can listen to closely or ignore. Bossa nova slowed samba down into something hushed, and the 'Moonlight' Sonata's slow, rippling first movement keeps that calm going.
input.confidence_reason: The catalog has a focused lo-fi track plus calm ambient, bossa nova and classical options. Only one song is tagged 'focused', and some calm picks are tagged melancholic rather than neutral.
